items.title: Peter Bocage Interview, 1959-01-29
items.q: So that's when Louis came from Chicago and went into Suburban Garden.

ctx.x: And then over on Tranchini opened another place in Metro. It's a church now, a great big place there on the highway. They converted it into a church. And we stayed there a while. Then we went to Suburban Garden for Jack Sheen. We worked there a couple years. And it was all with Piron. Yeah, all with Piron, yeah. And finally, Louis came down at Suburban Garden. Well, we were to go back in there, but we had a kind of misunderstanding between old man Tranchini and Piron. We didn't go, so they sat and got Louis in…
I was wondering about when you, how did you tell how old you were when you started in music on violin, taking lessons?

items.title: Peter Bocage Interview, 1962-02-06
items.q: he could play the horn nice, you know, like Louis, you know.

ctx.x: Do you remember any of the trumpet players like Buddy Petit and Chris Kelly?

Yeah, Chris Kelly, Buddy Petit, Rene, now he would have made a nice trumpet player that boy, if he hadn't got the proper schooling, you know. He was better than Buddy Petit. Rene, he was very good. But he was too much of a musician, but he could play the horn nice, you know, like Louis, you know. Had a nice time? Yeah, a nice, very nice time. What kind of jobs did he play? Nothing but dances, you know, like we played. Maybe one of the little nightclubs, you know. During the war he played down at the, what's the…
Not Larchens? No, no. Oh, no, that's on Almanaster. I can't think of that one.
